ops.name: page.add
ops.description: Add a page as a person does: its record and a first tree a visitor can see (its name as the heading of a first section), in one step; the core draws its id and answers `{ pageId }`. Give its name, its address, where it goes and the layout that frames it. It is shown at once (the next publish puts it live), and a section added later goes beside the first one. Use it rather than page.create and page.init, which a stored log and an import write. Refused with `unknown_page` (no such parent), `unknown_component` (no layout by that key), `page.slug` (a sibling holds the address, or it is reserved) and `route.taken`.

title.description: The page's name in the site's main language: what lists and menus show, and the heading of its first section.

slug.description: Its address segment: lower-case words joined by `-` (`studio`), or `[name]` for a dynamic segment.

slugs.description: Its address segment in other languages: language → slug; a language without one answers `slug`.

parentId.description: The page to put it under; absent or null: the top level.

anyOf.description: A page of the site: its id, as site_context lists the pages.

position.description: Its place among its siblings (lower first); absent: after the last.

layout.description: The key of a layout of the site that frames it (its header and footer); absent: the home page's layout; null: none.

declares.description: Leave it out: only a step stored before pages said which node holds their sections carries false.

ops.name: page.remove
ops.description: Delete a page as a person does: its record and its tree, in one step that undo puts back. Use it rather than page.delete and page.drop. Refused with `page.has_children` (pages sit under it: move or delete them first), `page.home` (the home page), `page.inMenu` (a menu links it: menuItem.remove first; detail.menus), `page.linked` (something links to it; detail.links), `page.notFoundPage` (the page shown at a missing address: settings.setNotFound first) and `unknown_page`.

pageId.description: A page of the site: its id, as site_context lists the pages.

ops.name: mixin.set
ops.description: Set or clear one of the site's mixins: a named style every node that lists it takes, so one edit changes them all. A mixin has a label and a style by scope (any scope but `p:` and `sub:`); nodes take it with tree.set_mixins; `mixin: null` clears it. Refused: `mixin.known` (clearing or breaking a mixin nodes still list: the refusal names them, take it off them first).

key.description: The mixin's key: lower-case letters, digits, - and _ (what tree.set_mixins lists).

propertyNames.description: When a style holds: `base` (always), or parts joined by `|`, all of which hold (`bp:md|s:hover`). Each part is `<prefix>:<value>`: `bp:<name>` from a breakpoint of the site up (mobile first; names such as sm, md, lg, xl are in the tokens read); `mq:<media query>` (`mq:(max-width: 767.98px)`, `mq:(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, `mq:(hover: none)`); `cq:<container query>`; `s:<state>` the node's own state (`s:hover`, `s:focus-visible`, `s:active`, `s:current`, `s:open`, `s:checked`, `s:empty`, `s:loaded`, `s:playing`), a state the page sets on nodes (`s:scene-active`, `s:step=2`), or selector terms (`s:::after`, `s::not([href])`, `s:[aria-expanded="true"]`); `a:<state>` the same state held by an ancestor (`a:hover`: the link or button around it is hovered); `pg:<state>=<value>` a page state, any of several values (`pg:menu=open`, `pg:menu=closed,open`); `p:<part>` a named part of the widget it is (`p:track`); `sub:<subset>` the items of a repeat subset; `st:enter` the style it starts from when it first shows; `sp:word` or `sp:char` each word or letter of a split text; `t:<selector>` its descendants (`t: a`, `t:> li`); `th:<theme>` where that theme applies; `fmt:<format>` when drawn in that output format.

mixin.description: { label, style }: its name and its declarations by scope key (any scope but p: and sub:); null clears it.

anyOf.description: A value the page reads when it renders: `$bind` names it. Inside a repeat, `item.<field>` (a field of the collection item), `item.$url`, `item.$index`, `item.$first`, `item.<reference>.<field>`; anywhere: `site.name`, `site.tagline`, `site.logo`, `page.title`, `page.excerpt`, `page.featuredImageId`, `page.authorName`, `page.publishedAt`, `list.$count`, `member.name`, `request.query.<name>`, `measured.lighthouse.performance`, `design.contrast` (with `pair`). `template` writes the value into words holding `{value}` (`Page {value}`); `fallback` is what shows when the value is missing.

A value the page reads when it renders: `$bind` names it. Inside a repeat, `item.<field>` (a field of the collection item), `item.$url`, `item.$index`, `item.$first`, `item.<reference>.<field>`; anywhere: `site.name`, `site.tagline`, `site.logo`, `page.title`, `page.excerpt`, `page.featuredImageId`, `page.authorName`, `page.publishedAt`, `list.$count`, `member.name`, `request.query.<name>`, `measured.lighthouse.performance`, `design.contrast` (with `pair`). `template` writes the value into words holding `{value}` (`Page {value}`); `fallback` is what shows when the value is missing.

__schema0.description: A value: CSS text or a number (`"1.5rem"`, `600`), a token (`{ "$token": "color.text" }`), a cell of the component (`{ "$cell": "<variant>.<size>.<state>.<part>.<bp>.<property>" }`), a prop of the component it is inside (`{ "$prop": "title" }`), a field of the repeat item around it (`{ "$item": "title" }`), a page state (`{ "$state": "menu" }`), a value the page reads when it renders (`{ "$bind": "item.title" }`), a choice on a prop or state (`{ "$switch": { "on": { "$prop": "tone" }, "cases": { "dark": "#111" } } }`) or a formatted value (`$format`).

ops.name: component.setPresence
ops.description: Make a part of a component present only while a prop holds a value or a condition on its props holds, or always present (null). An instance whose prop is empty then draws no such part: an eyebrow line, a button without a link. Refusals: `unknown_component`; the validator's `definition.presence` (a part or a prop the component lacks).

key.description: The component's key, as the site read lists its definitions (`component.project-card`, `region.header`).

part.description: The part's name, one of the component's parts.

prop.description: A prop name (present while it holds a value), `{ prop, is }` (while it equals one value or one of a list), `{ not }`, `{ all: [] }`, `{ any: [] }`; null: always present.

ops.name: theme.set
ops.description: Set or remove one theme of the site, whole: its label, the token sets it reads in order, whether it is a draft and where it applies by itself. A draft is offered to no page or section until published; `activation` applies it by colour scheme, host or address prefix. To change one field, send the theme as it stands with that field changed. Which theme is the default does not change by edit. Refused with `theme.default` (making another theme the default, clearing the default, or a draft or activation on the default) and `theme.known` (a token set the site lacks, which themeSet.set adds; or removing a theme a part or a style names).

key.description: The theme's key (`light`, `dark`), as the site read lists the themes; a new key adds a theme.

theme.description: The theme whole: `label`, `sets` (token set keys in order, a later one wins), `draft: true` to keep it off pages until published, `activation` ({ prefersColorScheme: light or dark, hostname, pathPrefix }: where it applies by itself), `isDefault` as it stands. Null removes it.

ops.name: themeSet.set
ops.description: Set or remove one token set a non-default theme reads, a DTCG token tree whose tokens win over the sets before it in the theme. The tree replaces the stored set. The default tokens are token.set's. Refused with `theme.known` (the key is a set of the default tokens, or a theme still reads the set being removed).

key.description: The token set's key (`semantic-dark`): one a theme lists in its `sets`, never a set of the default tokens.

tokens.description: The set whole, a DTCG token tree (groups of tokens with `$value` and `$type`); null removes it.

ops.name: site.setLocales
ops.description: Set the site's languages and, per language, the languages it reads before the main one when a text is missing. The main language is the one the texts are stored in and does not change here: send it as it is (site.setMainLocale makes another language the main one, its texts with it). A language dropped while pages hold its translations keeps them and reports `l10n.orphan`. Refused with `site.locales` (a changed main language, the main language missing from the list, a language twice, a fallback that is no site language, the main language or itself).

defaultLocale.description: The site's main language, as it is now (site.setMainLocale changes it); null only in an undo.

locales.description: Every language of the site, the main one among them: BCP 47 tags (`it`, `en`, `en-US`); null only in an undo.

fallbacks.description: Per language, the languages it reads in order before the main one when a text is missing there (`{ "en-US": ["en"] }`); absent or null: none.

ops.name: site.setMainLocale
ops.description: Make another of the site's languages its main one, in one step everywhere a text lives. Its translations become the site's own texts and the old main language becomes a translation, its words kept; a text it had no translation of keeps the old main language's words. Its addresses lose their language prefix and the old main language's take one; old addresses answer with a redirect. Dry-run it first and tell the person what it answers: output { was: the old main language, missing: how many texts kept the old words, places: where (kind, id, name, count) }. Refused: `site.mainLocale` (already the main language, or not one of the site's languages: add it with site.setLocales first).

locale.description: The language that becomes the main one: one of the site's languages (site_context locales) other than its main one.

ops.name: site.restoreMainLocale
ops.description: Put back every text, address and language setting a change of the site's main language wrote, as it was. Libretto writes it as the undo of site.setMainLocale; a batch that sends it is refused (only Libretto makes it). To change the main language again, send site.setMainLocale.

values.description: Each leaf the step wrote as it was, by document path (site, pages/<id>, content/<id>, navigation/<key>, collections/<id>/items/<id>, forms/<id>, media/<id>, settings/general); null: it was absent.

ops.name: guideline.set
ops.description: Set or clear one guideline rule: for a role, an op or op prefix and optionally a style property, whether it is fixed, free or a choice of tokens, with the note people read. A fixed rule refuses that role's batches with `guideline.fixed`; a choice rule refuses a style value outside its token group with `guideline.choice`. Where several rules match, the most specific wins (design system, then property, then op, then role), and fixed over choice over free. Discovery shows each op's verdict for the caller. A rule of null removes it. Refused: `invalid_input` (the stored guidelines are not rules).

rule.note: I colori del testo vengono dalla palette dello studio.
Le animazioni le cura il designer.

id.description: The rule's id: lowercase letters, digits and dashes; setting an id again replaces its rule.

rule.description: The rule, or null to remove it. role: a role (designer, editor) or "*"; op: an op name, a prefix ending in ".*" or "*"; property: the style property it governs; designSystem: true for ops that write the design system only; mode: "fixed", "free" or { choice: { tokens: <token group> } }; note: what the person reads.

ops.name: page.setHead
ops.description: Set or clear fields of a page's head, what search engines, link previews and the browser tab read. Its fields: title, meta title, description, social image, canonical address, noindex and structured-data subject. A field given is set, null clears it (the title cannot be cleared), a field left out is kept. A field's value in another language is a translation (translation.set, pointer `/head/<field>`). Refused with `head.image` (no such image in the media library, or an SVG or a video), `head.subject` (a subject reading fields the page's collection lacks, or on a page that is no dynamic page) and `unknown_page` (the page has no tree).

head.metaTitle: Archiplan — Studio di architettura a Roma
head.description: Restauro, residenziale, commerciale e culturale: spazi che bilanciano luce, materia e proporzione.

pageId.description: A page of the site: its id, as site_context lists the pages.

title.description: The page title the title template wraps for the browser tab and search results; it cannot be cleared.

metaTitle.description: The whole `<title>`, used as it is instead of the templated title; null clears it.

description.description: What search results and link previews say under the title; null: the site's default.

noIndex.description: True keeps the page out of search engines; null lets them in again.

ogImage.description: The picture a link preview shows: a media id of a raster image (no SVG); null: the site's default.

canonical.description: The address search engines should count the page under: an absolute http(s) URL; null clears it.

subject.description: What the page presents as structured data (schema.org): an Article, BlogPosting or TechArticle (on a dynamic page, the item fields it reads), a Product or a SoftwareApplication; written when the page has a canonical URL. Null clears it.

ops.name: site.setSeo
ops.description: Set the site's search defaults whole: the title template every page title goes in, and the description, social image and noindex of the pages that set none. Pages never copy them, so a change reaches every page at once. The object replaces the stored one (send every field you keep); null clears them all. Refused with `head.image` when the social image is no raster image of the media library.

seo.description: Archiplan, studio di architettura e interior design a Roma.

titleTemplate.description: The `<title>` every page gets: `%s` is the page title, `{site}` the site's name (`%s — {site}`).

description.description: The description of a page that sets none.

ogImage.description: The link-preview picture of a page that sets none: a media id of a raster image.

noIndex.description: True keeps every page out of search engines.

seo.description: The defaults, whole; null clears them.

ops.name: collection.create
ops.description: Add a collection to the site: its key (what repeats and dynamic pages name), its label and its fields, with no items yet. Add or change fields later with collection.setField and items with item.create or item.import. Refused: `collection.exists` (the id or the key is taken), `collection.field` (a field key listed twice, or a reference field naming a collection the site does not have).

id.description: A new uuid you choose for the collection: the id later ops name it by.

key.description: The collection's key, what repeats and dynamic pages name: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits, - or _.

label.description: What an editor reads: one line for every language, or one line per language ({ "it": "Progetti", "en": "Projects" }).

key.description: A field's key, what values and queries name: a letter, then letters, digits or _.

type.description: What the field holds: text, richtext, number, boolean, date, colour, media, link, list, json, reference, select, mediaList, file. A reference names its target collection, a select its options, a list its columns.

localized.description: true: an item holds one value per language ({ "it": …, "en": … }); false: one value for every language.

label.description: What an editor reads: one line for every language, or one line per language ({ "it": "Progetti", "en": "Projects" }).

required.description: Whether an item gives it a value before it goes live (the admin asks for it). Absent: as stored.

collection.description: A reference field's target collection, by key.

multiple.description: A reference field: true holds a list of item uids (at most 200), false or absent one.

label.description: What an editor reads: one line for every language, or one line per language ({ "it": "Progetti", "en": "Projects" }).

key.description: A field's key, what values and queries name: a letter, then letters, digits or _.

type.description: What the field holds: text, richtext, number, boolean, date, colour, media, link, list, json, reference, select, mediaList, file. A reference names its target collection, a select its options, a list its columns.

label.description: What an editor reads: one line for every language, or one line per language ({ "it": "Progetti", "en": "Projects" }).

ops.name: collection.set
ops.description: Rename a collection (its label or its key), or name the field that titles each item and the one its address is made from. titleField and slugField name a field of the collection; null takes the choice off. Fields left out stay as they are. Refused: `collection.unknown`, `collection.exists` (another collection has the key), `collection.inUse` (a new key while a repeat, a dynamic page or another collection's reference field reads the old one; detail.readers names them), `collection.field` (titleField or slugField names no field of it).

id.description: The collection, by its id (the data read lists each collection with its id and key).

key.description: The collection's key, what repeats and dynamic pages name: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits, - or _.

label.description: Its new label; null takes the label off (the key reads as its name).

anyOf.description: What an editor reads: one line for every language, or one line per language ({ "it": "Progetti", "en": "Projects" }).

titleField.description: A field of the collection, by key; null takes the choice off (the first text field titles the item).

anyOf.description: A field's key, what values and queries name: a letter, then letters, digits or _.

slugField.description: A field of the collection, by key; null takes the choice off (the first text field titles the item).

anyOf.description: A field's key, what values and queries name: a letter, then letters, digits or _.

ops.name: collection.remove
ops.description: Remove a collection that has no items and that nothing reads. Refused: `collection.unknown`, `collection.notEmpty` (it still has items: remove them with item.remove first), `collection.inUse` (a repeat, a dynamic page or another collection's reference field reads it; detail.readers names them).

id.description: The collection, by its id (the data read lists each collection with its id and key).

ops.name: collection.restore
ops.description: Put a collection's definition back whole as it was, its items untouched. Libretto writes it as the undo of collection.remove, collection.set and the field ops; a batch that sends it is refused (only Libretto makes it). On an undo it is refused with `collection.exists` when another collection took its key since.

id.description: The collection, by its id (the data read lists each collection with its id and key).

definition.description: The collection definition whole: { key, label, fields, titleField, slugField }.

ops.name: collection.setField
ops.description: Add one field to a collection, or change one: its type, whether it holds one value per language, its label, whether an item must give it, a list's columns or its place among the fields. A field with a key the collection has is changed, else added. A reference names its target collection (by key) and multiple, a select its options, a list its columns (fields). What the field stores beside what the op says (its help; its label, required and columns when not said) and the other fields stay as they are. Refused: `collection.unknown`, `collection.field` (over 200 fields, or a reference to a collection the site does not have), `item.value` (a reference or select changed so a value an item holds no longer fits: change those items with item.set first).

id.description: The collection, by its id (the data read lists each collection with its id and key).

key.description: A field's key, what values and queries name: a letter, then letters, digits or _.

type.description: What the field holds: text, richtext, number, boolean, date, colour, media, link, list, json, reference, select, mediaList, file. A reference names its target collection, a select its options, a list its columns.

localized.description: true: an item holds one value per language ({ "it": …, "en": … }); false: one value for every language.

label.description: What an editor reads: one line for every language, or one line per language ({ "it": "Progetti", "en": "Projects" }).

required.description: Whether an item gives it a value before it goes live (the admin asks for it). Absent: as stored.

collection.description: A reference field's target collection, by key.

multiple.description: A reference field: true holds a list of item uids (at most 200), false or absent one.

label.description: What an editor reads: one line for every language, or one line per language ({ "it": "Progetti", "en": "Projects" }).

key.description: A field's key, what values and queries name: a letter, then letters, digits or _.

type.description: What the field holds: text, richtext, number, boolean, date, colour, media, link, list, json, reference, select, mediaList, file. A reference names its target collection, a select its options, a list its columns.

label.description: What an editor reads: one line for every language, or one line per language ({ "it": "Progetti", "en": "Projects" }).

index.description: Its place among the fields, from 0; absent: where it is, or last for a new field.

rewriteAll.description: Leave it out: it marks entries an older version of the op stored, which rewrote every field.

ops.name: collection.removeField
ops.description: Remove one field from a collection; items keep the values they hold for it, unread, so putting the field back shows them again. The other fields stay as they are; a template that shows the field shows nothing there. Refused: `collection.unknown`, `collection.field` (no such field), `collection.inUse` (a repeat filters, sorts or picks by it; detail.readers names them).

id.description: The collection, by its id (the data read lists each collection with its id and key).

key.description: A field's key, what values and queries name: a letter, then letters, digits or _.

rewriteAll.description: Leave it out: it marks entries an older version of the op stored, which rewrote every field.

ops.name: item.create
ops.description: Add one item to a collection: its slug, its values by field, its status (draft unless said) and its place (last unless said). For many items at once send item.import. A value for a field the collection does not have is kept, unread. Refused: `collection.unknown`, `item.exists` (the id is taken), `item.slug` (another item has the slug), `item.value` (a value that does not fit its field: its type, a select's options, a reference's target items).

collection.description: The collection, by its id (the data read lists each collection with its id and key).

id.description: A new uuid you choose for the item: its uid.

slug.description: The item's address under its collection's page: lowercase letters, digits and -, unique in the collection; or one per language ({ "it": "casa-sul-lago", "en": "lake-house" }).

status.description: draft (kept off the live site) or published (live with the next publish).

position.description: Its place among the items: lower comes first.

propertyNames.description: A field's key, what values and queries name: a letter, then letters, digits or _.

values.description: Values by field key. A per-language field takes one value per locale ({ "en": …, "it": … }). A richtext field takes a text (read as paragraphs split on blank lines) or prose blocks { children, nodes }: children lists the top-level node ids in order, nodes maps each id (8 lowercase letters or digits) to its node. Blocks: a paragraph or heading { kind: "text", as: "p" | "h2"…"h6", runs } and a code block (as "pre"); a quote { kind: "frame", as: "blockquote", children: [paragraphs] }; a list { kind: "frame", as: "ul" | "ol", start?, children: [{ kind: "text", as: "li", runs } or { kind: "frame", as: "li", children: [paragraphs, lists] }] }; a figure { kind: "frame", as: "figure", children: [{ kind: "image", src: { $media }, alt }, then optionally { kind: "frame", as: "figcaption", children: [paragraphs] }] }. A run is words, { t, m: marks } or { br: true }; marks: strong, em, u, s, mark, sub, sup, code, kbd, { a: { href, target?, label? } } (href http(s), mailto, tel, a path or #fragment; label is its aria-label), { span: { lang?, id? } } (id an anchor a #link leads to, once per value). No style, attributes, binds or anchors on a node; at most 500 top blocks and 5000 nodes. Paragraph with a list: { "children": ["para0001", "list0001"], "nodes": { "para0001": { "kind": "text", "as": "p", "runs": ["Read ", { "t": "the essay", "m": [{ "a": { "href": "/the-essay" } }, "em"] }] }, "list0001": { "kind": "frame", "as": "ul", "children": ["item0001"] }, "item0001": { "kind": "text", "as": "li", "text": "One point" } } }. Figure: "fig00001": { "kind": "frame", "as": "figure", "children": ["img00001", "cap00001"] }, "img00001": { "kind": "image", "src": { "$media": "<media id>" }, "alt": "A bridge" }, "cap00001": { "kind": "frame", "as": "figcaption", "children": ["capt0001"] }, "capt0001": { "kind": "text", "as": "p", "text": "The bridge" }. Footnote: the call { "t": "1", "m": [{ "a": { "href": "#fn1", "label": "Note 1" } }, { "span": { "id": "ref1" } }, "sup"] } in a paragraph; the note, an li of an ol: { "kind": "text", "as": "li", "runs": [{ "t": "Source.", "m": [{ "span": { "id": "fn1" } }] }, " ", { "t": "↩", "m": [{ "a": { "href": "#ref1", "label": "Back to note 1" } }] }] }. A value outside this is refused (item.value), naming the first offending node.

ops.name: item.set
ops.description: Change one item: some of its values (null clears one), its slug, its status (draft or published) or its place in the collection. Values and fields left out stay as they are. Refused: `collection.unknown`, `item.unknown`, `item.field` (a value for a field the collection does not have: add it with collection.setField), `item.value` (a value that does not fit its field), `item.slug` (another item has the slug).

collection.description: The collection, by its id (the data read lists each collection with its id and key).

id.description: The item, by its uid (the data read lists each item with it).

propertyNames.description: A field's key, what values and queries name: a letter, then letters, digits or _.

A richtext field takes a text (read as paragraphs split on blank lines) or prose blocks { children, nodes }: children lists the top-level node ids in order, nodes maps each id (8 lowercase letters or digits) to its node. A run is words, { t, m: marks } or { br: true }; marks: strong, em, u, s, mark, sub, sup, code, kbd, { a: { href, target?, label? } } (href http(s), mailto, tel, a path or #fragment; label is its aria-label), { span: { lang?, id? } } (id an anchor a #link leads to, once per value). No style, attributes, binds or anchors on a node; at most 500 top blocks and 5000 nodes. Paragraph with a list: { "children": ["para0001", "list0001"], "nodes": { "para0001": { "kind": "text", "as": "p", "runs": ["Read ", { "t": "the essay", "m": [{ "a": { "href": "/the-essay" } }, "em"] }] }, "list0001": { "kind": "frame", "as": "ul", "children": ["item0001"] }, "item0001": { "kind": "text", "as": "li", "text": "One point" } } }. Figure: "fig00001": { "kind": "frame", "as": "figure", "children": ["img00001", "cap00001"] }, "img00001": { "kind": "image", "src": { "$media": "<media id>" }, "alt": "A bridge" }, "cap00001": { "kind": "frame", "as": "figcaption", "children": ["capt0001"] }, "capt0001": { "kind": "text", "as": "p", "text": "The bridge" }. Footnote: the call { "t": "1", "m": [{ "a": { "href": "#fn1", "label": "Note 1" } }, { "span": { "id": "ref1" } }, "sup"] } in a paragraph; the note, an li of an ol: { "kind": "text", "as": "li", "runs": [{ "t": "Source.", "m": [{ "span": { "id": "fn1" } }] }, " ", { "t": "↩", "m": [{ "a": { "href": "#ref1", "label": "Back to note 1" } }] }] }. A value outside this is refused (item.value), naming the first offending node.

slug.description: The item's address under its collection's page: lowercase letters, digits and -, unique in the collection; or one per language ({ "it": "casa-sul-lago", "en": "lake-house" }).

status.description: draft (kept off the live site) or published (live with the next publish).

position.description: Its place among the items: lower comes first.

ops.name: item.remove
ops.description: Remove one item from a collection. Refused: `collection.unknown`, `item.unknown`, `item.referenced` (another item references it; detail.referrers names them: clear those references with item.set first).

collection.description: The collection, by its id (the data read lists each collection with its id and key).

id.description: The item, by its uid (the data read lists each item with it).

ops.name: item.restore
ops.description: Put one item back whole as it was (its record as stored, references checked). Libretto writes it as the undo of item.set, item.remove and item.revert; a batch that sends it is refused (only Libretto makes it). To bring an item back as an earlier step left it, send item.revert.

collection.description: The collection, by its id (the data read lists each collection with its id and key).

id.description: The item, by its uid (the data read lists each item with it).

item.description: The item record whole: { uid, slug, status, position, values }.

ops.name: item.import
ops.description: Add many items to a collection in one step, all of them or none (a file's rows, at most 500). Each row: a new id, its slug, status (draft unless said) and values by field; the rows go after the items there, in order. Each row is checked as item.create checks one, and a value for a field the collection does not have is refused (`item.field`). Refused: `collection.unknown`, `item.exists`, `item.slug` (a slug taken, by an item or an earlier row), `item.value`, `item.field`; each refusal names its row (detail.row, from 1).

collection.description: The collection, by its id (the data read lists each collection with its id and key).

id.description: A new uuid you choose for the item: its uid.

slug.description: The item's address under its collection's page: lowercase letters, digits and -, unique in the collection; or one per language ({ "it": "casa-sul-lago", "en": "lake-house" }).

status.description: draft (kept off the live site) or published (live with the next publish).

propertyNames.description: A field's key, what values and queries name: a letter, then letters, digits or _.

values.description: Values by field key. A per-language field takes one value per locale ({ "en": …, "it": … }). A richtext field takes a text (read as paragraphs split on blank lines) or prose blocks { children, nodes }: children lists the top-level node ids in order, nodes maps each id (8 lowercase letters or digits) to its node. Blocks: a paragraph or heading { kind: "text", as: "p" | "h2"…"h6", runs } and a code block (as "pre"); a quote { kind: "frame", as: "blockquote", children: [paragraphs] }; a list { kind: "frame", as: "ul" | "ol", start?, children: [{ kind: "text", as: "li", runs } or { kind: "frame", as: "li", children: [paragraphs, lists] }] }; a figure { kind: "frame", as: "figure", children: [{ kind: "image", src: { $media }, alt }, then optionally { kind: "frame", as: "figcaption", children: [paragraphs] }] }. A run is words, { t, m: marks } or { br: true }; marks: strong, em, u, s, mark, sub, sup, code, kbd, { a: { href, target?, label? } } (href http(s), mailto, tel, a path or #fragment; label is its aria-label), { span: { lang?, id? } } (id an anchor a #link leads to, once per value). No style, attributes, binds or anchors on a node; at most 500 top blocks and 5000 nodes. Paragraph with a list: { "children": ["para0001", "list0001"], "nodes": { "para0001": { "kind": "text", "as": "p", "runs": ["Read ", { "t": "the essay", "m": [{ "a": { "href": "/the-essay" } }, "em"] }] }, "list0001": { "kind": "frame", "as": "ul", "children": ["item0001"] }, "item0001": { "kind": "text", "as": "li", "text": "One point" } } }. Figure: "fig00001": { "kind": "frame", "as": "figure", "children": ["img00001", "cap00001"] }, "img00001": { "kind": "image", "src": { "$media": "<media id>" }, "alt": "A bridge" }, "cap00001": { "kind": "frame", "as": "figcaption", "children": ["capt0001"] }, "capt0001": { "kind": "text", "as": "p", "text": "The bridge" }. Footnote: the call { "t": "1", "m": [{ "a": { "href": "#fn1", "label": "Note 1" } }, { "span": { "id": "ref1" } }, "sup"] } in a paragraph; the note, an li of an ol: { "kind": "text", "as": "li", "runs": [{ "t": "Source.", "m": [{ "span": { "id": "fn1" } }] }, " ", { "t": "↩", "m": [{ "a": { "href": "#ref1", "label": "Back to note 1" } }] }] }. A value outside this is refused (item.value), naming the first offending node.

items.description: The rows, in the order they go after the items there.

ops.name: item.revert
ops.description: Bring one item back as an earlier step left it: its record (slug, status, values) whole, in one step. Its place among the items stays as the draft has it. Use it for an item that is still in the draft; a removed item comes back through the undo of its removal. Refused: `collection.unknown`, `item.unknown` (the item is not in the draft), `item.revertMissing` (detail: missing field or item, and their names) when the record holds a value for a field the collection no longer has, or a reference names an item that is gone.

collection.description: The collection, by its id (the data read lists each collection with its id and key).

id.description: The item, by its uid (the data read lists each item with it).

item.description: The item record as the earlier step left it: { uid, slug, status, values } (its position is not read). document/<version> holds the collections as a version left them.

ops.name: menu.create
ops.description: Add a menu: its key (what a header, a footer or a page names to show it), its name in the editor and, optionally, its first items and its place among the menus. Refused with `menu.exists` (the key is taken), `menu.target` (an item leads to a page the site lacks), `menu.pageTwice` (one page linked twice), `menu.nesting` (a column title on a top-level item) and `menu.invalid` (too many items, an item id twice).

key.description: The new menu's key: lower-case words joined by `-` (`footer-legal`); what a header, footer or page names to show it.

label.description: The menu's name in the editor; visitors never read it.

items.description: Its first items, in order.

A menu item: `id` (8 characters of [0-9a-z], unique in the menu), `label` (words, or language → words) and `target`: a page (`{ kind: "page", pageId }`), a named place on a page (`{ kind: "anchor", pageId, anchor }`), an outside or site address (`{ kind: "external", href }`: https://, mailto:, tel: or /path) or the language switch (`{ kind: "languages" }`). A top-level item may hold `children` (one level); a child may hold `group`, the column title of a wide menu.

position.description: Its place among the site's menus; absent: last.

ops.name: menu.rename
ops.description: Change a menu's name in the editor; its key, what pages and layouts name, stays. Refused with `menu.unknown`.

key.description: A menu of the site: its key (`main`, `footer`), as the `navigation` read lists the menus.

label.description: The menu's name in the editor; visitors never read it.

ops.name: menu.delete
ops.description: Delete a menu nothing shows. Refused with `menu.inUse` when a page, a layout or a component reads it (point them at another menu first) and `menu.unknown`.

key.description: A menu of the site: its key (`main`, `footer`), as the `navigation` read lists the menus.

ops.name: menuItem.add
ops.description: Add one item to a menu: at the top level, or under a top-level item (`parent`), at `index` (absent: last). Refused with `menu.pageTwice` (the menu already links that page), `menu.target` (no such page), `menu.nesting` (an item with children under a parent, a column title at the top level, no such parent), `menu.invalid` (an id the menu holds, too many items) and `menu.unknown`.

menu.description: A menu of the site: its key (`main`, `footer`), as the `navigation` read lists the menus.

item.description: A menu item: `id` (8 characters of [0-9a-z], unique in the menu), `label` (words, or language → words) and `target`: a page (`{ kind: "page", pageId }`), a named place on a page (`{ kind: "anchor", pageId, anchor }`), an outside or site address (`{ kind: "external", href }`: https://, mailto:, tel: or /path) or the language switch (`{ kind: "languages" }`). A top-level item may hold `children` (one level); a child may hold `group`, the column title of a wide menu.

parent.description: The top-level item to put it under; null or absent: the top level.

anyOf.description: A menu item's id: 8 characters of [0-9a-z], unique in its menu (the `navigation` read lists them).

index.description: Its place among the items there (0 first); absent: last.

ops.name: menuItem.remove
ops.description: Remove an item from a menu, with the items under it. Refused with `menu.unknownItem` and `menu.unknown`.

menu.description: A menu of the site: its key (`main`, `footer`), as the `navigation` read lists the menus.

id.description: A menu item's id: 8 characters of [0-9a-z], unique in its menu (the `navigation` read lists them).

ops.name: menuItem.move
ops.description: Move a menu item to another place: the top level, or under a top-level item (`parent`), at `index` (absent: last); the items under it move with it. Refused with `menu.nesting` (an item with children under another, an item under itself, a column title at the top level), `menu.unknownItem` and `menu.unknown`.

menu.description: A menu of the site: its key (`main`, `footer`), as the `navigation` read lists the menus.

id.description: A menu item's id: 8 characters of [0-9a-z], unique in its menu (the `navigation` read lists them).

parent.description: The top-level item to put it under; null or absent: the top level.

anyOf.description: A menu item's id: 8 characters of [0-9a-z], unique in its menu (the `navigation` read lists them).

index.description: Its place among the items there (0 first); absent: last.

ops.name: menuItem.update
ops.description: Change a menu item's words, where it leads or its column title (null clears the title); a field left out is kept. Refused with `menu.pageTwice` (the menu already links the new page), `menu.target` (no such page), `menu.nesting` (a column title on a top-level item), `menu.unknownItem` and `menu.unknown`.

menu.description: A menu of the site: its key (`main`, `footer`), as the `navigation` read lists the menus.

id.description: A menu item's id: 8 characters of [0-9a-z], unique in its menu (the `navigation` read lists them).

label.description: Its words, or language → words.

target.description: Where it leads, whole: `{ kind: "page", pageId }`, `{ kind: "anchor", pageId, anchor }`, `{ kind: "external", href }` or `{ kind: "languages" }`.

group.description: A child's column title in a wide menu; null clears it. A top-level item takes none.

ops.name: redirect.add
ops.description: Add a redirect to the site's list: from a path of the site, or a path and everything under it, to a path of the site or an https address, with status 301 or 302. The server answers a redirect before any page. Refused with `redirect.duplicate` (that source has a rule already, a trailing slash ignored), `redirect.loop` (the chain leads back to one of its sources), `redirect.hidesPage` (the source is the address of a published page) and `redirect.invalid` (the list is full, or a rule is malformed).

redirect.description: A redirect: `from`, a path of the site starting with / (end it with /* for the path and everything under it), `to`, a path of the site or an https:// address, and `status`, 301 (moved for good) or 302 (for now).

index.description: Its place in the list (0 first); absent: last.

ops.name: redirect.update
ops.description: Change the redirect from source `from`: its source, target or status, the rule given whole as `redirect`. Refused with `redirect.unknown` (no rule from that source) and the checks redirect.add makes (`redirect.duplicate`, `redirect.loop`, `redirect.hidesPage`, `redirect.invalid`).

from.description: The source of the redirect to change, as the `redirects` read lists them (a trailing slash is ignored).

redirect.description: A redirect: `from`, a path of the site starting with / (end it with /* for the path and everything under it), `to`, a path of the site or an https:// address, and `status`, 301 (moved for good) or 302 (for now). Given whole.

ops.name: redirect.remove
ops.description: Remove the redirect from source `from` (a trailing slash ignored). Refused with `redirect.unknown`.

from.description: The source of the redirect to change, as the `redirects` read lists them (a trailing slash is ignored).

ops.name: settings.setNotFound
ops.description: Name the page a visitor sees, with status 404, at an address no page answers: one page, and optionally another per language. Null goes back to the built-in page. Refused with `notFound.page` (no such page, a page with no tree, or the home page) and `notFound.locale` (a language the site does not have).

notFound.description: `pageId`, a page of the site (site_context lists them), and `locales`, language → another page for that language; null: the built-in page.

ops.name: settings.setGeneral
ops.description: Set or clear the site values pages show (its name, tagline, company name, support e-mail and legal line) and its pictures (its icon and the logo search engines show). A field given is set, null clears it, a field left out is kept. Refused with `settings.picture` when a picture's media id is not in the media library or is no image or SVG.

siteName.description: The site's name: what headers, footers and page titles show; null clears it.

siteDescription.description: The site's tagline; null clears it.

companyName.description: The company behind the site, as footers and legal lines show it; null clears it.

supportEmail.description: The e-mail address pages show for contact; null clears it.

legalLine.description: The legal line a footer shows (company number, VAT); null clears it.

favicon.description: The site's icon (browser tab, phone home screen): a media id of an image or an SVG, or a file URL; null clears it.

organizationLogo.description: The logo search engines show for the site (absent: the icon): a media id of an image or an SVG, or a file URL; null clears it.

ops.name: breakpoint.set
ops.description: Set or clear one breakpoint: the media query a `bp:<name>` style scope stands for. To rename one, use breakpoint.rename, which rewrites every style that names it. Refused with `breakpoint.shadowed` (another token set holds it: edit it there), `breakpoint.unknown` (clearing one the set lacks) and `scope.known` (clearing a breakpoint a style still names).

name.description: The breakpoint's name: what a `bp:<name>` style scope names (`md`, `wide-desktop`).

query.description: The media query it stands for: `(min-width: 768px)`, `print`, `screen and (min-width: 1024px)`; null clears the breakpoint.

set.description: The token set that holds it; absent: `breakpoints`, where the site keeps them.

ops.name: breakpoint.rename
ops.description: Give a breakpoint another name, in one step: every style scope, component cell, motion, picture source and token value that names it names the new one. Refused with `breakpoint.taken` (the new name is `base` or another breakpoint's), `breakpoint.shadowed` (another token set holds it: rename it there), `breakpoint.fixed` (a document viewer spreads from it by name) and `breakpoint.unknown`.

to.description: Its new name: lower-case words joined by `-`, not `base` and no other breakpoint's.

set.description: The token set that holds it; absent: `breakpoints`, where the site keeps them.

ops.name: form.create
ops.description: Add a form to the site: its key, label, fields and settings. Its submissions go to the inbox; to make them also file an access request, send form.setAction after it. A page shows the form through a form section or widget that names its id. Refused: `form.exists` (the id is taken), `form.keyTaken` (another form has the key), `form.action` (an action other than the inbox), `form.invalid` (the form breaks a rule: field keys unique, replyToField an email field).

id.description: A new uuid you choose for the form.

form.description: The form: key (lowercase words joined by -, unique on the site, never changed later), label, fields (at least one, at most 40) and settings: recipients (emails notified of each submission), replyToField (an email field), consent, honeypot, minFillMs, open, action { kind: "inbox" }, messages, summary, marker.

ops.name: form.update
ops.description: Change a form's label or its settings: who is notified, the checks a submit runs, the words around them. Settings given replace the stored ones whole, all but the action (form.setAction sets it); its key and fields stay (the formField ops change fields). Refused: `form.unknown`, `form.invalid` (the form would break a rule: replyToField names no email field of it).

id.description: The form, by its id (the forms read lists the site's forms).

label.description: Its new label: one text, or one per locale.

settings.description: Its settings whole, all but the action: recipients, senderName, replyToField, consent, honeypot, minFillMs, open, messages, summary, marker; what is left out takes its default.

ops.name: form.setAction
ops.description: Set what a stored submission of a form also does: inbox (nothing more) or accessRequest (files a workspace request with the platform admins from the fields its map names). It reaches people outside the site, so only the site's administrator sets it. Refused: `form.unknown`, `form.invalid` (the map names a field the form does not have, an email that is not an email field, or a name or email field that is not required).

id.description: The form, by its id (the forms read lists the site's forms).

action.description: { kind: "inbox" }: nothing more; { kind: "accessRequest", fields: { name, email, studio?, website?, message? } }: files a workspace request with the platform admins, each key naming the form field that fills it.

ops.name: form.delete
ops.description: Delete a form that no page, layout, component or item names; its submissions stay in the inbox. Refused: `form.unknown`, `form.inUse` (something still shows it; the refusal names up to three: take the form off them first), `form.invalid` (a stored form that does not read).

id.description: The form, by its id (the forms read lists the site's forms).

ops.name: formField.add
ops.description: Add a field to a form, at a place among its fields (last unless said). Refused: `form.unknown`, `form.invalid` (its key is another field's, or the form would hold over 40 fields).

form.description: The form, by its id (the forms read lists the site's forms).

field.description: The field whole: key, type (text, email, tel, textarea, select, checkbox, date), label (one text or one per locale), required, and optionally help, placeholder, maxLength, showCount, pattern (text and tel), options (a select's { value, label }) and its own messages { required, invalid }.

index.description: Its place among the fields, from 0; absent: last.

ops.name: formField.update
ops.description: Replace one field of a form whole: its type, label, help, checks, options and messages; its key may change. Send every property it keeps: what the new field leaves out is gone. Refused: `form.unknown`, `form.unknownField` (no field of that key), `form.invalid` (the new key is another field's, or a field replyToField or the access request names stops fitting).

help.en: Place, timing and a rough budget.

form.description: The form, by its id (the forms read lists the site's forms).

key.description: The field, by its key.

field.description: The field whole as it becomes (its key may change): what it leaves out is gone.

ops.name: formField.move
ops.description: Move one field of a form to another place among its fields. Refused: `form.unknown`, `form.unknownField` (no field of that key).

form.description: The form, by its id (the forms read lists the site's forms).

key.description: The field, by its key.

index.description: Its new place among the fields, from 0.

ops.name: formField.remove
ops.description: Remove one field from a form; submissions already stored keep what it held. Refused: `form.unknown`, `form.unknownField` (no field of that key), `form.invalid` (its last field, or the field replyToField or the access request names).

form.description: The form, by its id (the forms read lists the site's forms).

key.description: The field, by its key.

ops.name: memberRole.create
ops.description: Add a member role the site's members can hold, with its key and its label. Add it before a page's access (page.setAccess) or a part's audience (tree.set_audience) names it; memberRole.rename changes the label of one that exists. Giving the role to a member is not an op. Refused: `memberRole.exists` (the site has a role with that key). Output: the role at memberRoles/<key>.

key.description: The role key: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter, up to 40 characters. Pages (page.setAccess `requiredRoles`), parts (tree.set_audience `roles`) and members name the role by it.

label.description: The name people see: one text, or a text per locale ({ it: "Clienti", en: "Clients" }), up to 60 characters each.

ops.name: memberRole.rename
ops.description: Change the label of a member role; its key stays, so the pages, parts and members that name it keep it. To change the key, create a role with the new key, move the pages and parts onto it, then delete the old one. Refused: `memberRole.unknown` (the site has no role with that key). Output: the role at memberRoles/<key> with its new label.

key.description: The role key: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter, up to 40 characters. Pages (page.setAccess `requiredRoles`), parts (tree.set_audience `roles`) and members name the role by it.

label.description: The name people see: one text, or a text per locale ({ it: "Clienti", en: "Clients" }), up to 60 characters each.

ops.name: memberRole.delete
ops.description: Delete a member role that no page's access and no part's audience names. Take the role off those first (page.setAccess, tree.set_audience), so a page or a part never opens to every member when a role goes. Refused: `memberRole.unknown` (the site has no role with that key), `memberRole.inUse` (pages or parts still name it; the message lists them). Output: memberRoles/<key> removed.

key.description: The role key: lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter, up to 40 characters. Pages (page.setAccess `requiredRoles`), parts (tree.set_audience `roles`) and members name the role by it.

ops.name: version.snapshot
ops.description: Name the site as it is now: a version to publish, compare with or return to. It changes nothing on the site, and undo does not take it back. Refused with `version.exists` when the name is taken.

examples.name: Nuovo sito 2026
examples.note: Nuova home, pagina Persone e i lavori di via Giulia

name.description: The version's name, as a person calls it (`Nuovo sito 2026`): at most 64 characters, used once, never `live`.

note.description: What the version holds, in a few words, for whoever reads the list of versions.

ops.name: tree.duplicate
ops.description: Copy a part and everything under it right after itself, under fresh ids, with the motion wholly inside it. Use it for a part inside a section or a card (a paragraph, a picture, a column); copy a whole section with section.insert from a page, and a list's item with slot.add. The copy is named `name` when given; an anchor is not copied; motion that also reaches outside the part stays behind, named in a `motion.left_behind` finding (`motion: false` copies none). Refused: `duplicate.not_a_part` (the tree's root, or a part a list or a repeat holds; for a list's item the sentence names the slot.add with `source: { copy }` that copies it), `op_target` (no such node). Output: { root } of the copy.

at.description: Which tree the node is in: `{ page: <pageId> }` for a page's own tree (ids in site_context pages), or `{ component: <key> }` for a definition's own tree (a component, or the header, footer or layout that frames pages; keys in site_context definitions). A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page.

node.description: The part to copy: a node of the tree `at` names, whose parent is a frame, group or vector (node/<pageId>?node= reads it).

name.description: The copy's own name in Structure; absent: the name the part has.

motion.description: false: the motion wholly inside the part stays where it is (none copied or taken); absent: it goes with the part.

ops.name: section.insert
ops.description: Add a section to a page: a new instance of a section component of the site, or a copy of a section of a page. It goes after section `after` or before section `before` (neither: at the end). From a component it shows its defaults and the values `source.props` gives; a copy from a page brings the motion wholly inside it (`motion: false`: none) and names motion it cannot bring in a `motion.left_behind` finding. A kind the site has not used yet is section.addKind, a saved part preset.insert. Refused: `section.not_a_section`, `section.component` (not a section component), `section.layout`, `unknown_component`, `section.no_holder`, `instance.required_prop` (a required prop left out). Output: { root } of the new section.

at.description: The page: { page: <pageId> } (site_context lists the pages).

after.description: The section of the page the new one goes right after.

before.description: The section of the page the new one goes right before; with neither, at the end.

component.description: The key of a definition marked a section (the sections read lists them, with the props each needs).

props.description: Values of the new section's props by name; a prop it cannot be drawn without and has no default for must be given.

page.description: The page the section to copy is on.

node.description: The section to copy: one of that page's sections.

name.description: The copy's own name; absent: the name the section has.

source.description: What the new section is: a new instance of a section component, or a copy of a section of a page.

motion.description: false: the motion wholly inside the part stays where it is (none copied or taken); absent: it goes with the part.

declares.description: Leave it out: only a step stored before pages said which node holds their sections carries false.

ops.name: section.move
ops.description: Move a section of a page to another place among its sections, with everything it holds. It goes right after section `after` or right before section `before`; with neither, to the end of the page. Only whole sections move this way: a part inside a section moves with tree.move. Refused: `section.not_a_section` (`node`, `after` or `before` is not a section; for a part inside one, the refusal names that section), `invalid_input` (beside itself), `op_target` (no such node), `section.no_holder`.

at.description: The page: { page: <pageId> } (site_context lists the pages).

node.description: The section: one of the page's sections (a child of the node that holds them).

after.description: The section it goes right after.

before.description: The section it goes right before; with neither, to the end.

declares.description: Leave it out: only a step stored before pages said which node holds their sections carries false.

ops.name: section.remove
ops.description: Remove a section of a page with everything it holds, its translations and the motion wholly inside it, with the waits on that motion. `motion: false` leaves the motion, `waits: false` the waits. A part inside a section goes with tree.remove. Refused: `section.not_a_section`, `op_target` (no such node), `lock.removed` (a locked section: tree.set_locked unlocks it), `motion.starts_from_wait` (a timeline that stays starts from a wait it would take). Output: { took: { timelines, states, locks } } of the motion it took (`locks`: the gates that held the page's scroll), else null.

at.description: The page: { page: <pageId> } (site_context lists the pages).

node.description: The section: one of the page's sections (a child of the node that holds them).

motion.description: false: the motion wholly inside the part stays where it is (none copied or taken); absent: it goes with the part.

waits.description: false: the waits on its motion stay (a gate that opens when one of its timelines ends).

declares.description: Leave it out: only a step stored before pages said which node holds their sections carries false.

ops.name: section.holder
ops.description: Say which node of a page holds its sections: its children are the page's sections, what the section ops move, copy and remove. `node` is a frame, group or vector of the page; no `node` takes the statement off, and the page is read by its shape. A new page states its root, and a section op states the holder on an older page that states none, so this is rarely needed. Refused: `unknown_page` (`at` is a definition), `op_target` (no such node).

at.description: The page: { page: <pageId> } (site_context lists the pages).

node.description: The frame, group or vector of the page whose children are its sections; absent: the page states none.

ops.name: component.setSection
ops.description: Mark a component as a section a person adds to a page (`section: true`), or unmark it. Only a marked component is offered among the sections and taken by section.insert; a layout never is. What it draws does not change. Refused: `unknown_component` (no such definition).

key.description: The definition's key (site_context lists the definitions).

ops.name: section.addKind
ops.description: Add a section of one of the kinds every site can add to a page, though its design system has none: text-and-picture, questions-and-answers, contact-form, banner, gallery or cards. It goes right after section `after`, right before section `before`, else at the end. The first time, its definition `kind.<kind>` joins the design system in the site's tokens (a contact form also adds a form when the site has none); after that section.insert of `kind.<kind>` adds another. A list kind starts with a few items in the site's language. Refused: `section.not_a_section`, `section.no_holder`. Findings: `kind.colours`, a colour pair of the site the kind could not use. Output: { root } of the new section.

at.description: The page: { page: <pageId> } (site_context lists the pages).

after.description: The section of the page the new one goes right after.

before.description: The section of the page the new one goes right before; with neither, at the end.

props.description: Values of the new section's props by name; usually none.

ops.name: slot.add
ops.description: Add an item to a list of a component instance (a carousel's slides, a list's items, a grid's cards): slot `slot` of instance `node`, at `index` (absent: at the end). The item is a copy of one of the slot's items (`source.copy`, under fresh ids, with its translations, not its motion), or nodes of its own (`source.root` and `source.nodes`). Use it rather than instance.fillSlot, which replaces a slot's whole content. Refused: `slot.full` (the slot holds its most items), `slot.not_a_list`, `slot.unknown`, `slot.no_item` (the item to copy is not in the slot), `duplicate_id`, `orphan_node`, `invalid_input` (an index past the end). Output: { root } of the new item.

at.description: Which tree the node is in: `{ page: <pageId> }` for a page's own tree (ids in site_context pages), or `{ component: <key> }` for a definition's own tree (a component, or the header, footer or layout that frames pages; keys in site_context definitions). A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page.

node.description: The component instance that holds the list (node/<pageId>?node= reads its slots).

slot.description: The list's slot name, as the instance's definition declares it (definition/<key> lists its slots).

index.description: Where the item goes among the slot's items, from 0; absent: at the end.

copy.description: An item of the slot to copy, under fresh ids.

name.description: The copy's own name; absent: the name the item has.

root.description: The new item's root: one of `nodes`.

propertyNames.description: A node id: 8 characters of a-z and 0-9, unique in its tree (read them in page/<pageId> and node/<pageId>?node=<nodeId>). A node you add takes an id you make up that its tree does not hold yet.

When a style holds: `base` (always), or parts joined by `|`, all of which hold (`bp:md|s:hover`). Each part is `<prefix>:<value>`: `bp:<name>` from a breakpoint of the site up (mobile first; names such as sm, md, lg, xl are in the tokens read); `mq:<media query>` (`mq:(max-width: 767.98px)`, `mq:(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, `mq:(hover: none)`); `cq:<container query>`; `s:<state>` the node's own state (`s:hover`, `s:focus-visible`, `s:active`, `s:current`, `s:open`, `s:checked`, `s:empty`, `s:loaded`, `s:playing`), a state the page sets on nodes (`s:scene-active`, `s:step=2`), or selector terms (`s:::after`, `s::not([href])`, `s:[aria-expanded="true"]`); `a:<state>` the same state held by an ancestor (`a:hover`: the link or button around it is hovered); `pg:<state>=<value>` a page state, any of several values (`pg:menu=open`, `pg:menu=closed,open`); `p:<part>` a named part of the widget it is (`p:track`); `sub:<subset>` the items of a repeat subset; `st:enter` the style it starts from when it first shows; `sp:word` or `sp:char` each word or letter of a split text; `t:<selector>` its descendants (`t: a`, `t:> li`); `th:<theme>` where that theme applies; `fmt:<format>` when drawn in that output format.

anyOf.description: A value the page reads when it renders: `$bind` names it. ops.name: slot.move
ops.description: Move an item of a component instance's list to another place among the slot's items, with everything it holds. `index` is the place it takes, from 0, counted among the items. Refused: `slot.no_item` (not an item of the slot), `slot.not_a_list`, `slot.unknown`, `invalid_input` (an index past the last item).

at.description: Which tree the node is in: `{ page: <pageId> }` for a page's own tree (ids in site_context pages), or `{ component: <key> }` for a definition's own tree (a component, or the header, footer or layout that frames pages; keys in site_context definitions). A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page.

node.description: The component instance that holds the list (node/<pageId>?node= reads its slots).

slot.description: The list's slot name, as the instance's definition declares it (definition/<key> lists its slots).

item.description: The item to move: one of the slot's items.

index.description: The place it takes among the slot's items, from 0.

ops.name: slot.remove
ops.description: Remove an item from a component instance's list with everything it holds, its translations and the motion wholly inside it, with the waits on that motion (a gate that opens when one of its timelines ends). `motion: false` leaves that motion, `waits: false` the waits. Refused: `slot.at_least` (the slot would hold fewer than its least items), `motion.starts_from_wait` (a timeline that stays starts from a wait it would take), `slot.no_item`, `slot.not_a_list`, `slot.unknown`. Output: { took: { timelines, states, locks } } of the motion it took, else null.

at.description: Which tree the node is in: `{ page: <pageId> }` for a page's own tree (ids in site_context pages), or `{ component: <key> }` for a definition's own tree (a component, or the header, footer or layout that frames pages; keys in site_context definitions). A part of the header shown on every page is in its definition, not on the page.

node.description: The component instance that holds the list (node/<pageId>?node= reads its slots).

slot.description: The list's slot name, as the instance's definition declares it (definition/<key> lists its slots).

item.description: The item to remove: one of the slot's items.

motion.description: false: the motion wholly inside the item stays where it is; absent: it goes with the item.

waits.description: false: the waits on its motion stay (a gate that opens when one of its timelines ends).

ops.name: format.create
ops.description: Add a format to the site: a box a canvas page is drawn in, in one unit, with optional margins, safe insets, bleed and its own output profile. A canvas lists the formats it is drawn in with surface.set. Refused: `format.exists` (the key is taken: format.update changes it), `format.profile` (its profile is not one of the site's: outputProfile.create adds it).

key.description: The format's key: lower-case letters, digits, - and _ (a canvas's surface and its fmt: scopes name it).

format.description: The format whole: its label, width and height in its unit (px, mm, pt or in), and optional margins, safe insets, bleed and own output profile.

ops.name: format.update
ops.description: Replace a format of the site whole; the canvases drawn in it keep it and are drawn in its new box. Refused: `format.unknown` (no such format), `format.profile` (its profile is not one of the site's).

key.description: The format's key: lower-case letters, digits, - and _ (a canvas's surface and its fmt: scopes name it).

format.description: The format whole: its label, width and height in its unit (px, mm, pt or in), and optional margins, safe insets, bleed and own output profile.

ops.name: format.remove
ops.description: Remove a format of the site. Refused: `format.inUse` (a canvas lists it, or a component's style has a fmt: scope for it: the refusal names them), `format.unknown` (no such format).

key.description: The key of the site's format or output profile.

ops.name: outputProfile.create
ops.description: Add an output profile to the site: how an image or a print output of a canvas is made. An image profile gives the file type and its scale or ppi; a print profile is PDF/X-4, with its printing condition and what a colour without an ink does (`refuse` or `convert`). Refused: `outputProfile.exists` (the key is taken: outputProfile.update changes it).

intent.condition: Offset su carta patinata, PSO Coated v3

key.description: The profile's key: lower-case letters, digits, - and _ (a format and a canvas's outputs name it).

profile.description: The profile whole: medium image (type png, jpeg or webp, a scale or a ppi, a quality for a lossy type) or medium print (PDF/X-4: its printing condition, what a colour without ink does, ink limit, image ppi, marks).

ops.name: outputProfile.update
ops.description: Replace an output profile of the site whole; the canvases and formats that take it keep it. Refused: `outputProfile.unknown` (no such profile).

key.description: The profile's key: lower-case letters, digits, - and _ (a format and a canvas's outputs name it).

profile.description: The profile whole: medium image (type png, jpeg or webp, a scale or a ppi, a quality for a lossy type) or medium print (PDF/X-4: its printing condition, what a colour without ink does, ink limit, image ppi, marks).

ops.name: outputProfile.remove
ops.description: Remove an output profile of the site. Refused: `outputProfile.inUse` (a canvas builds an output with it, or a format takes it as its own: the refusal names them), `outputProfile.unknown` (no such profile).

key.description: The key of the site's format or output profile.

ops.name: surface.set
ops.description: Set a canvas page's surface whole: the formats it is drawn in, its master format and the outputs built when the site is published. The master is the format its base styles are written for; the others override them in fmt:<key> scopes. Each output is a format and an output profile. Refused: `surface.canvas` (the page is not a canvas), `surface.formats` (a format or profile the site does not have), `scope.format` (a format dropped while the canvas still styles it), `unknown_page`. Findings: `output.ink`, a warning for each colour it paints with no print ink when one of its outputs prints.

pageId.description: The canvas page's id (site_context lists the pages).

surface.description: The surface whole: formats (keys of the site's formats), master (one of them) and outputs ({ format, profile } pairs, built at publish).

ops.name: output.check
ops.description: Read the print findings of a canvas: each colour it paints that has no ink in a print profile of its outputs. `output.ink` is an error where the profile refuses such a colour (that print is not made) and a warning where it converts it. `format` narrows it to one of the canvas's formats; `profile` asks about a profile of the site the canvas does not build yet. A read: it changes nothing. Refused: `output.notCanvas`, `output.format` (the canvas is not drawn in that format), `outputProfile.unknown`, `unknown_page`. Output: { findings }.

pageId.description: The canvas page's id.

format.description: Only this one of the canvas's formats; absent: all of them.

profile.description: Judge with this profile of the site on each format, even one the canvas does not build yet; absent: the outputs it builds.

ops.name: contrast.correct
ops.description: Set a text's colour in one scope to a colour that passes AA on its ground: the correction the contrast check writes itself when a batch settles, with the pair, both colours and both ratios. No one sends it: Libretto writes it, and a batch that carries it is refused as reserved. An undo runs it back. To fix a pair yourself, set the text's colour with tree.set_style or instance.override; contrast/<pageId> lists the pairs. Refused: `contrast.uncorrectable` (the text is not a page node or an inner node of an instance on the page).

pageId.description: The page the pair is on (site_context lists the pages; contrast/<pageId> reads its pairs).

ops.name: contrast.correctLayout
ops.description: Set the colour of a layout's own text (in its header or footer), in one scope, to a colour that passes AA on its ground: the correction the contrast check writes when a batch settles. It carries the page it was measured on, the pair, both colours and both ratios. No one sends it: Libretto writes it, and a batch that carries it is refused as reserved. An undo runs it back. Refused: `contrast.uncorrectable` (`key` is not a layout, or the text is not one of its own).

scope.description: When a style holds: `base` (always), or parts joined by `|`, all of which hold (`bp:md|s:hover`). Each part is `<prefix>:<value>`: `bp:<name>` from a breakpoint of the site up (mobile first; names such as sm, md, lg, xl are in the tokens read); `mq:<media query>` (`mq:(max-width: 767.98px)`, `mq:(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`, `mq:(hover: none)`); `cq:<container query>`; `s:<state>` the node's own state (`s:hover`, `s:focus-visible`, `s:active`, `s:current`, `s:open`, `s:checked`, `s:empty`, `s:loaded`, `s:playing`), a state the page sets on nodes (`s:scene-active`, `s:step=2`), or selector terms (`s:::after`, `s::not([href])`, `s:[aria-expanded="true"]`); `a:<state>` the same state held by an ancestor (`a:hover`: the link or button around it is hovered); `pg:<state>=<value>` a page state, any of several values (`pg:menu=open`, `pg:menu=closed,open`); `p:<part>` a named part of the widget it is (`p:track`); `sub:<subset>` the items of a repeat subset; `st:enter` the style it starts from when it first shows; `sp:word` or `sp:char` each word or letter of a split text; `t:<selector>` its descendants (`t: a`, `t:> li`); `th:<theme>` where that theme applies; `fmt:<format>` when drawn in that output format.

ops.name: contrast.bypass
ops.description: Keep a text and ground pair as it is although it fails AA or cannot be measured: a record on the page of who, when, the ratio it measures and why. It is a person's decision, the site administrator's: an agent cannot send it, and asks a person to accept the pair in Libretto, or fixes the colour instead. Text "*" keeps every text on a ground that cannot be measured (a moving, blended or pictured ground), through later text edits. A second bypass of a pair replaces its record. Refused: `contrast.unknown_pair` (the page has no such pair, or the ground makes no text unmeasurable), `contrast.unmeasured`, `unknown_page`.

text.description: The text's id as contrast/<pageId> names it (an instance's inner text: <instance>-<node>); "*": every text on the ground.

ground.description: The ground's id as contrast/<pageId> names it, or canvas: the page itself.

reason.description: Why the pair stays as it is, in the words people read in History and on the page's checks.

ops.name: contrast.unbypass
ops.description: Take the bypass off a pair: the next write that touches the page judges the pair again and corrects it if it fails. Like contrast.bypass, it is the site administrator's alone; an agent cannot send it. Refused: `op_target` (the pair has no bypass).

pageId.description: The page the pair is on (site_context lists the pages; contrast/<pageId> reads its pairs).

text.description: The text's id as contrast/<pageId> names it (an instance's inner text: <instance>-<node>); "*": every text on the ground.

ground.description: The ground's id as contrast/<pageId> names it, or canvas: the page itself.

ops.name: contrast.restoreBypass
ops.description: Put a bypass record back as it was: the undo of contrast.bypass, contrast.unbypass and contrast.dropBypass, replacing the pair's record when it has one. No one sends it: Libretto writes it, and a batch that carries it is refused as reserved.

pageId.description: The page the pair is on (site_context lists the pages; contrast/<pageId> reads its pairs).

ops.name: contrast.dropBypass
ops.description: Take the bypass record off a pair whose node left the page: the contrast check writes it in the batch that removes the node. No one sends it: Libretto writes it, and a batch that carries it is refused as reserved. Undoing that batch puts the record back (contrast.restoreBypass). Refused: `op_target` (the pair has no bypass).

pageId.description: The page the pair is on (site_context lists the pages; contrast/<pageId> reads its pairs).

text.description: The text's id as contrast/<pageId> names it (an instance's inner text: <instance>-<node>); "*": every text on the ground.

ground.description: The ground's id as contrast/<pageId> names it, or canvas: the page itself.

ops.name: component.acceptContrast
ops.description: Accept a text and ground pair that fails AA or cannot be measured for every instance of a component, from a page where an instance shows it. It is a person's decision, the site administrator's: an agent cannot send it, and asks a person to accept the pair in Libretto, or fixes the colour instead. An instance reads the pair as accepted while it measures as it did here. To keep a pair on one page only, a person uses contrast.bypass. Refused: `contrast.not_in_component` (text and ground are not both inside one instance), `contrast.unknown_pair`, `unknown_component`, `duplicate_key` (already accepted), `unknown_page`.

text.description: The text as contrast/<pageId> names it (<instance>-<node>), or "*": every text on a ground the component paints.

ground.description: The ground as contrast/<pageId> names it, inside the same instance.

reason.description: Why the pair stays as it is, in the words people read in History and on the component.

ops.name: component.unacceptContrast
ops.description: Take back the acceptance of a pair on a component, named by the component's own node ids: the next write that changes the pair on a page judges it again. Like component.acceptContrast, it is the site administrator's alone; an agent cannot send it. Refused: `op_target` (the pair is not accepted).

key.description: The component that holds the acceptance (component.<name>).

text.description: The text's id inside the component (its own node id, not the page's <instance>-<node>), or "*".

ground.description: The ground's id inside the component.

ops.name: component.restoreAcceptance
ops.description: Put an acceptance back on a component as it was: the undo of component.unacceptContrast and component.dropAcceptance, which Libretto runs when that batch is undone. No one sends it: Libretto writes it, and a batch that carries it is refused as reserved. Refused: `duplicate_key` (the pair is accepted already), `unknown_component`.
